[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
The current profile gives Margaret an exact birth date of 19 March 1734. Two derivative transcripts instead label that day as her baptism at Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, and give only birth year 1734; the inherited exact birth day is unresolved. The entry names father Andrew Glasgow and mother Isobel Clerk. The selected link to [[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]] is a 79% probable adult identification, because his asserted 1714-child-to-adult bridge remains unproved; the attached mother [[Clerk-314|Isobel Clerk]] is retained without a separate assessed adult-profile identity.
== Research Notes ==
The earlier proposal described Margaret without qualification as the daughter of Glasgow-1336 and Clerk-314. That is retained as prior profile history; the transcript establishes the named Andrew/Isobel record roles, while the adult-profile identifications remain separate. The inherited 19 March exact birth field is not validated by these baptism transcripts.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1336]] is assessed at 79% (probable). The held 1734 FamilySearch citation identifies Isobel Clerk but does not reproduce the father field. Two saved Findmypast companion transcripts name Andrew Glasgow and Isobel Clerk at Margaret’s 19 March 1734 Kirknewton baptism. That establishes the recorded parent roles for this child event; identifying the adult Andrew with the 1714 child Glasgow-1336 remains unproved.

Existing child-to-father link assessed from held public evidence; the recorded Andrew/Isobel parent roles are now explicit in derivative baptism transcripts; no evidence bridges adult Andrew to the 1714 child Glasgow-1336. Retain this complete-profile identity limit.

The saved 1734 child event is distinct from the household’s 1732 Margaret account, whose presumed early death remains unproved. Birth year is indexed, while 19 March is explicitly the baptism date. The two Findmypast transcripts are companion derivatives, not independent originals; the register image has not been inspected.

Next useful test: Inspect the original Kirknewton 1732 and 1734 entries and seek evidence linking adult Andrew to the 1714 child Glasgow-1336; the 1732 Margaret’s estimated early death remains unproved.

Source basis already held: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-NBH "Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-NBH : 12 February 2020), Isobel Clerk in entry for Margaret Glasgow, 1734.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
